data.gender_notes: Wandie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Andreia', meaning 'manliness, bravery, or strength'. Wandie is a female form, often interpreted as 'Ruler of the People'. In the New Testament, Saint Andrew was a disciple of Jesus, and his sister, Saint Andrew the Apostle, is venerated as a patron saint of Greece. The name Wandie carries the meaning “Ruler of the People” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Wandie usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying courage and leadership.
data.etymology: Wandie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Wandie total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: וַנְדִיא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew root נָדַח (nadach) meaning ‘to desire, to be gracious, to show favor, to be merciful, to repent’. The name Wandie can be interpreted as ‘desirable’, ‘wishing’, or ‘one who shows favor’.

in_greek.name: Ανδρέα
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Wandie in Greek is transliterated from the Hebrew name as 'Andreas'. The original Hebrew name 'Wandie' is not directly represented in the Greek language as it has a different origin and meaning.

in_latin.name: Wandia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Wandie in Latin is derived from the Hebrew name and transliterated as 'Wandia'. It retains the original Hebrew meaning of ‘desirable, wishing, or one who shows favor’.

in_english.name: Wandie
in_english.long_meaning: The name Wandie in English has the same meaning as its original Hebrew form, which is ‘desirable, wishing, or one who shows favor’.
